label: lem:block
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Block update

title: Proof
body_md:
During the cycle the same stepsize $1/\mu_\ell$ is used.  On the $a$- and
$b$-eigenspaces the one-step multipliers are respectively
$1-a/\mu_\ell=(\mu_\ell-a)/\mu_\ell$ and
$1-b/\mu_\ell=-(b-\mu_\ell)/\mu_\ell$.  Taking the $m$th powers gives
\eqref{eq:block-update}.
head: environment

label: thm:classification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:classification}
Let $A=aP+bQ$ with $0<a<b$ and $P,Q$ orthogonal projectors of nonzero rank,
$P+Q=I$, and $PQ=0$.
For CSD with an integer cycle length $m\ge2$, consider any initial error
$e_0$ and let $g_0=Ae_0$.  If $g_0=0$, then $x_0=x_*$ and no step is taken.
Otherwise exactly one of the following holds.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If $Pg_0=0$ or $Qg_0=0$, the method reaches $x_*$ after one update.
\item If both blocks are nonzero and
$\lVertPg_0\rVert_2=\lVertQg_0\rVert_2$, then every update uses
$\alpha=2/(a+b)$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:equal-orbit}
  \lVerte_{k+1}\rVert_2=\rho\lVerte_k\rVert_2,
  \qquad \rho=\frac{b-a}{b+a}\in(0,1).
\end{equation}
Thus the orbit is nonterminating and $R$-linear but not $R$-superlinear.
\item If both blocks are nonzero and
$\lVertPg_0\rVert_2\ne\lVertQg_0\rVert_2$, then the complete CSD sequence converges
$R$-superlinearly to $x_*$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the nonterminating non-$R$-superlinear initial gradients are
exactly the cone
\[
  \mathcal E=\{g\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|Pg\|=\|Qg\|>0\}.
\]
This cone has Lebesgue measure zero.
Since $A$ is invertible, the corresponding exceptional set of initial errors
and initial points is Lebesgue-null as well.
head: environment
name: Two-spectrum classification

label: eq:mu-components
title: Proof
body_md:
The first assertion follows because an initial gradient in one eigenspace is
annihilated by the exact step $1/a$ or $1/b$.

Assume henceforth that both blocks are nonzero.  Since $a<\mu_\ell<b$,
neither block multiplier vanishes, so both blocks remain nonzero at every
update.  From
\eqref{eq:rdef},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mu-components}
  \mu_\ell-a=\frac{b-a}{r_\ell^2+1},
  \qquad
  b-\mu_\ell=\frac{(b-a)r_\ell^2}{r_\ell^2+1}.
\end{equation}
Combining Lemma~\ref{lem:block} with \eqref{eq:mu-components} yields the
exact cycle-boundary recurrence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ratio-recurrence}
  r_{\ell+1}=r_\ell^{1-2m}.
\end{equation}

If $r_0=1$, then $\mu_\ell=(a+b)/2$ for every $\ell$, and each one-step
multiplier has modulus $\rho=(b-a)/(b+a)$.  The two blocks retain equal norm,
and $e_k=A^{-1}g_k$ is multiplied blockwise by the same factors.  Hence
\eqref{eq:equal-orbit} holds, proving the second assertion.

Suppose $r_0\ne1$ and put $q=2m-1\ge3$ and
$s_\ell=|\log r_\ell|$.  Equation~\eqref{eq:ratio-recurrence} gives
$s_\ell=q^\ell s_0$.  Let $G_\ell=\|g_{m\ell}\|$.  A direct use of
\eqref{eq:block-update} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta}
 \frac{G_{\ell+1}^2}{G_\ell^2}
 =\frac{(b-a)^{2m}(r_\ell^2+r_\ell^{4m})}
 {(a r_\ell^2+b)^{2m}(r_\ell^2+1)}.
\end{equation}
There is a constant $C=C(a,b,m)$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta-bound}
  \frac{G_{\ell+1}}{G_\ell}
  \le C\min\{r_\ell,r_\ell^{-1}\}=C e^{-s_\ell}.
\end{equation}
Indeed, for $r\le1$ use $r^2+r^{4m}\le2r^2$ and
$a r^2+b\ge b$; for $r\ge1$ use
$r^2+r^{4m}\le2r^{4m}$ and $a r^2+b\ge a r^2$.
Iterating \eqref{eq:theta-bound},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:superexp}
  G_\ell\le G_0 C^\ell
  \exp\!\left(-s_0\frac{q^\ell-1}{q-1}\right).
\end{equation}
Thus $G_\ell^{1/\ell}\to0$.  Between cycle boundaries there are only $m-1$
updates and all their multipliers are bounded by a constant depending on
$a,b$; consequently the full gradient sequence has root factor zero as well.
Since $a\lVerte_k\rVert_2\le\lVertg_k\rVert_2\le b\lVerte_k\rVert_2$, the same is true for the
error sequence.  This proves $R$-superlinear convergence in the third case.

Finally, $\mathcal E$ is contained in the zero set of the quadratic form
$g\mapsto\|Pg\|^2-\|Qg\|^2=g^{\mathsf{T}}(P-Q)g$, which is not identically zero
because $P$ and $Q$ have nonzero rank; the zero set of a nonzero polynomial
has Lebesgue measure zero.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The recurrence also explains why the cycle length matters.  For $m=1$ the
exponent in \eqref{eq:ratio-recurrence} is $-1$, so the ratio merely
alternates and ordinary exact-line-search steepest descent remains linear on
the equal-norm orbit.  The superlinear conclusion above uses $m\ge2$.
head: environment

label: cor:threshold
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:threshold}
The fixed instance $n=m=2$, $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)$,
zero linear term $c=0$, and $x_0=(1,1/3)^{\mathsf{T}}$ from~\cite{liwang2026} lies on the
equal-norm cone.  Hence Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} recovers its
nonterminating $R$-linear orbit with factor $1/2$, and the universal
$R$-superlinear assertion at $m\ge\left\lceil(n+1)/2\right\rceil$ is false.
head: environment
name: Threshold failure

title: Proof
body_md:
Here $g_0=Ax_0=(1,1)^{\mathsf{T}}$ has equal nonzero spectral-block norms.
Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} therefore gives a nonterminating orbit with
factor $(3-1)/(3+1)=1/2$.
